definition: an imaginary creature in stories that can change from a person into a wolf

collocations.example: In the legend, the man turns into a werewolf at night.
They watched an old werewolf movie on Halloween.

definition: a common light plastic used to make bags, bottles, and packaging

collocations.example: The store packs vegetables in a thin polyethylene bag.
These food containers are made of polyethylene.

definition: to make a short sound with a horn, whistle, or similar device

collocations.example: The driver tooted the horn to warn the children.
The small train tooted loudly as it left the station.

definition: a tight piece of underwear worn around the waist and hips to shape the body

collocations.example: She wore a girdle under her dress for a smoother look.
The tight girdle made it hard for her to breathe.

definition: to cut off a branch or part of something with one quick stroke

collocations.example: The gardener lopped off the dead branch with a saw.
We lopped back the bushes along the narrow path.

definition: a serious disease that makes the muscles stiff, often caused by a dirty wound

collocations.example: The nurse gave him a tetanus shot after the injury.
You can get tetanus from a rusty nail.

definition: a chemical that an animal produces to affect the behavior of others of its kind

collocations.example: Some insects release a pheromone to attract a mate.
Ants follow a pheromone signal to find food.

definition: a chess piece shaped like a castle tower that moves in straight lines

collocations.example: She moved the rook across the board to protect the king.
He captured a rook with his bishop in one move.

definition: fat under the skin that makes it look lumpy, often on the thighs and hips

collocations.example: The cream claims to reduce cellulite on the legs.
Many people have visible cellulite and it is completely normal.

definition: a person who cares too much about small rules and details

collocations.example: He is a real pedant about correct grammar.
I don't want to sound like a pedant, but that is wrong.

definition: relating to the shape and physical features of the land in an area

collocations.example: Hikers used a topographical map to plan the route.
Engineers did a topographical survey before building the road.

definition: a mathematical expression that adds together terms made of numbers and variables

collocations.example: Students learned to solve a polynomial in algebra class.
The teacher wrote a polynomial equation on the board.

definition: looking tired and thin, usually because of worry, illness, or lack of sleep

collocations.example: She looked haggard after working three night shifts.
His haggard face showed how little he had slept.

definition: full of twists, turns, and bends

collocations.example: The bus slowly climbed the tortuous mountain road.
The river follows a tortuous course through the valley.

definition: the ability of different systems or products to work together

collocations.example: The update will improve interoperability between the two systems.
We tested the interoperability between devices from different brands.

definition: a medical examination of the inside of the large intestine using a thin camera

collocations.example: Doctors advised him to have a colonoscopy after fifty.
A routine colonoscopy can help detect problems early.

definition: a short introduction at the beginning of a book, often written by someone else

collocations.example: A famous author wrote the foreword to her novel.
The editor thanked her team in the foreword.

definition: a dull gray metal made mostly of tin, used for cups, plates, and ornaments

collocations.example: He drank cider from an old pewter mug.
The small statue was made of pewter.

definition: describing a type of fat, found in some oils and fish, that is better for health

collocations.example: Fish contains polyunsaturated fat that is good for the heart.
She cooks with polyunsaturated oil instead of butter.

definition: a collection of documents and information about a person, event, or subject

collocations.example: The reporter compiled a dossier on the company's finances.
Police kept a detailed dossier on the suspect.

definition: very dirty and unpleasant, especially because of poverty or neglect

collocations.example: The refugees lived in squalid conditions for months.
The abandoned house looked squalid and smelled awful.

definition: a particular level or class within a society

collocations.example: People from every social stratum attended the public meeting.
The reforms mainly helped a lower stratum of society.

definition: a firm yellow or white cheese with a strong taste

collocations.example: She grated some sharp cheddar over the pasta.
He put a slice of cheddar on his sandwich.

definition: the state of not being respected or trusted by people

collocations.example: The old method has fallen into disrepute among doctors.
His behavior brought the whole team into disrepute.

definition: to help or encourage someone to do something wrong, especially a crime

collocations.example: She was accused of helping to aid and abet the thieves.
Anyone who abets a crime can also be punished.
